stem:
Esha studies the whole-number list $1$, $4$, $9$, $16$, $\ldots$

Which claim correctly continues the list using its generative rule?

options.text: Each term is the square of $1$, $2$, $3$, $4$, $\ldots$, so the next term is $25$.
The list looks neat, so no generative rule is needed to continue it.
Writing $25$ is what produces the earlier terms $1$, $4$, $9$, $16$.
The same rule also requires a cube-number formula before the list can continue.

teacher.key_rationale: The list is square numbers, so the next term after 16 is 25. Neat looks alone omit the generative rule. Saying 25 creates the earlier terms reverses the relation. Requiring a cube formula over-extends the hinge.
